### Summary

Every number this report quotes comes from a committed check. This section is the index of those checks: what each
one checks, how to run it, what it needs, and where its committed output is. It complements Appendix C
(@sec-appc), which lists pyharp's own `ctest` tests at the pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One table of every executable check in the report, with its command and output file.

**Data.** Check scripts and their committed outputs.

**Placement.** Run by hand, by an author before proposing a chapter; not run by the report's CI.

**Activation.** None.

**Guarantee / limits.** Lists the checks present in the report's tree; rows are added as chapters merge.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-index.
:::

Local symbols: none.

Checks come in two kinds. Those under `src/pyharp_report/chNN/checks/` verify a chapter's derivations with numpy
or sympy and do not import pyharp. Those under `derivation-checks/chNN/` run pyharp itself, or read the pyharp
tree, and record the build they ran against.

### Derivation

None: this section is an index and has no equations.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch10-index-flow shows where each kind of evidence comes from and where the chapters cite it. A check prints
one line per claim with a stable label (`[C1]`, `[S3]`, ...), and its output is committed next to it, so a
chapter can quote a label and a reader can rerun the command and compare.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-index-flow
#| fig-cap: "Where the report's numbers come from. pyharp's own tests (left) are run by ctest and by the CI job; the report's checks (right) are derivation checks in numpy or sympy and checks that run pyharp; their committed outputs are what the Tests layers of the chapters cite."
#| fig-alt: "Two columns of boxes. Left: pyharp tests feeding ctest and pytest, then the CI job. Right: numpy/sympy derivation checks and pyharp-running checks, both writing committed .out files, which arrows connect to the chapters' Tests layers."
#| echo: false
from pyharp_report.ch10.figures.fig_index_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the verification index. {#tbl-ch10-index-code}

The checks themselves are files of this report, not of pyharp, and are listed in the Tests layer below by path.

1. Run a numpy/sympy check with `python3 src/pyharp_report/chNN/checks/<scheme>_check.py` from `doc/tech-report`.
2. Run a pyharp check as its `derivation-checks/chNN/README.md` or header says, against a build of the pin. For this
   chapter, `derivation-checks/ch10/setup_env.sh <dir> <pydisort version>` builds each environment from public sources
   and `bash derivation-checks/ch10_run.sh <env 1.7.1> <env 1.8.13> <scratch dir>` regenerates every output above
   and the chapter's figures.

: Executable checks of the report in this tree. {#tbl-ch10-index-checks}

Each check writes its output next to it (`test_inventory.out`, `run_suite.<pairing>.out`, `abi_matrix.out`,
`bindings_diff.<pydisort>.out`, `header_diff.out`, `flaky_rerun.out`, `invariants.out`, `opacity_probe.out`,
`model_probe.out`, `floor_inventory.out`, `break_tests.out`); `test_inventory.py` and `bindings_diff.py` need a pyharp tree at the pin, and the
latter and `run_suite.sh` a build of it. All of them run and produce the outputs cited in @sec-ch10-test-suite,
@sec-ch10-packaging, @sec-ch10-bindings and @sec-ch10-invariants[^ch10-index-run]. The check of @sec-ch01-quickstart writes
`check_ch01_quickstart_pydisort171.out` and `_pydisort1813.out` and is regenerated by
`bash derivation-checks/ch01_run.sh <env 1.7.1> <env 1.8.13>`.

### Limits

- **Coverage of the index.** It lists the checks committed in this tree. Each chapter's checks join it when that
  chapter merges; until then a chapter's own Tests layer is the reference.
- **Not run by CI.** The report's CI renders the book and runs its tool tests; it does not rerun the checks, so a
  committed output can go stale against the pin. The pin is moved only with `code_anchors.py bump`, after which
  the outputs must be regenerated and the claims that cite them re-read.
